title: Neural Stored-program Memory with Mirror function codes
hypothesis: A small function-space code can combine shared controller programs into many useful logical linear programs and generalize to unseen codes with lower serialized memory than independent programs; private function variation reveals the capacity limit.
physical_object: Four shared linear controller basis programs stored in program memory
mirror_coordinate: Per-program coefficient vector addressing/interpolating shared controller programs
logical_multiplicity: 16/64 stored programs and 16 unseen code-composed functions

task.metric: Held-out input output NRMSE, unseen-code execution NRMSE, pairwise function uniqueness, actual complete program-memory payload bytes
task.router: Program key IDs are supplied and charged; held-out coefficient codes are runtime inputs

controls: Independent full linear program matrix per stored program
Neural Stored-program Memory with four explicit basis controllers and program coefficient values
Mirror rank-4 PCA function basis plus per-program codes
Native PCA rank-4 control with identical decoder
One-hot nearest-program selection without coefficient interpolation
success_gate: At residual 0 and both program counts, Mirror stored-program and unseen-code NRMSE <=0.02 and complete payload <=50% of independent programs. Mirror-specific success also requires strict gain over native PCA and NSPM basis/code controls.
failure_gate: Mirror misses held-out program quality/bytes or exactly aliases native PCA/NSPM basis coding without strict Mirror-specific gain. Fresh seeds remain sealed.
boundaries: No neural controller, dynamic interpolation training, or paper NSPM reproduction
Unseen function count is credited only through measured held-out execution quality
All basis/controller payloads and runtime codes are accounted
Runtime unseen codes are mapped into the learned basis coordinate system using a charged transform stored in the program payload.
